get_back: And their regret isn't about losing you. It's about losing what they had from you, the warmth that used to come their way without being asked for. That isn't the same thing as you.
They're trying to get you back, ⟦FIRST⟧.

And part of you is glad to hear it. Don't skip past that, and don't be ashamed of it either. I'm going to stay on it a minute, because of everything in these twelve cards, this is the part to watch closest.

Here's what their wish is really for. They don't want you. They want what used to come their way from you, pointed back at them again: the warmth, the way you let them land. They're holding your softness out with their hand open, waiting for you to walk all the way over and take it, so you'll be standing close enough to give it to them again.

They won't come down that path. A wish like theirs stays where it is and waits. It doesn't take a step.

I told you you'd need to know which way this went, because one way it's a gift and the other way it's a snare, and the words sound the same either way. It's the snare. Every kind thing in their letter is going to read like a reason to go to them. It isn't one.
They didn't leave. They came right up to the table and stayed there, closer than they'd been all night. I'd have given a good deal to have them back over by the door.

So they hold it out and they want you to come to them. I told you, back in the first letter, what it means when someone holds a thing out like that, and this is it. They won't take one step toward you. They want you to take all of them.
Their letter ends with an ask. They want something from you in the last line. I've left it in. Do nothing with it.
Come back. Or if you won't, at least write me back.
I left their ask in so you'd see it for what it is. It's a bill, and nobody owes it, least of all you.
